info.title: haau3 Platform API
info.description: The haau3 platform API is in preview: it may change as we build, usually to add features or improve performance. Endpoints require an API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Requests without a valid key return 401. Create a key in the dashboard at https://platform.haau3.com; a new organization starts on the free Developer plan. From 2026-11-02 a request past one of its plan's limits (requests a minute on every plan, requests a month on Developer) returns 429 with `Retry-After`. Every error under `/v1/fhir` is a FHIR `OperationOutcome` and every other error an RFC 9457 problem; https://docs.haau3.com/errors lists every status, whether to retry it, and what a method a path does not take answers.

tags.name: Scheduling
tags.description: Provider availability (SMART Scheduling Links): slots and publishers.

tags.name: FHIR base
tags.description: What the FHIR R4 base at `/v1/fhir/r4` answers for every service on it: the `CapabilityStatement` that lists them all, and batch Bundles that carry several requests to any of them in one round trip.

tags.name: Terminology
tags.description: FHIR terminology operations over the code systems listed in TerminologyCapabilities. Some are resolved from their own source when you ask; others are held here at a named release, which that resource also names.

tags.name: Provider directory
tags.description: CMS's National Provider Directory as FHIR R4: practitioners and their roles, organizations, payers and insurance networks, network membership, healthcare services, locations and endpoints. Every parameter the service serves is declared here, and any other is refused by name rather than ignored.

tags.name: Questionnaires
tags.description: FHIR Questionnaire, served as its source publishes it. This service holds copies of a curated set and reaches any other questionnaire its source publishes by canonical URL, as well as forms published at their own address under places this service is set up to reach. Read one by id, and build the QuestionnaireResponse in your own application.

tags.name: Medical Benefits
tags.description: FHIR InsurancePlan: what a Medicare Advantage or ACA Marketplace plan covers and what a member pays, read from the files CMS publishes. Every plan names the CMS release it was read from. Read a plan by its id, or search by identifier, name, state or county, and check whether the CMS National Provider Directory lists providers in a plan's network.

tags.name: Pharmacy Benefits
tags.description: The CARIN Consumer Real-Time Pharmacy Benefit Check as FHIR messaging: what a medication would cost a member under their coverage, or its price at pharmacies near a ZIP code, in real time, from the sources this service connects to. A member's request receives patient data, so send it only under an executed agreement.

tags.name: MedList
tags.description: One reconciled medication list from one patient's FHIR medication records, as US Core MedicationRequests with a Provenance for each. This operation receives patient data, so send it only under an executed agreement.

tags.name: Sandbox
tags.description: The FHIR base without production behind it, to build and test against: the same paths at `/v1/sandbox/fhir/r4`, answered with synthetic data that always gives the same answer. Its first service is the CARIN Consumer Real-Time Pharmacy Benefit Check, answered by Example Health Plan, a test insurer. It takes a test key (`haau3_sk_test_…`), made on the API keys page, and each request counts like any other. Send test members only, never a real person.

get.description: Returns the matching slots grouped by provider location: each item in `providerLocations` is one provider at one location, or a location with no provider, with its total slot count and soonest availability, paginated by provider location. Its opaque `key` drills down to its individual slots via `GET /v1/scheduling/slots?providerLocationKey=<key>`. Same filters as `/slots`. Requires a valid API key.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Slot availability state to return. Defaults to `free`.

parameters.name: publisher
parameters.description: Filter to a single publisher (source) by slug, such as `zocdoc` or `defacto`. See `GET /v1/scheduling/publishers` for the available slugs.

parameters.name: serviceTypeCode
parameters.description: Filter by service type code (as published by the source). A slot matches when any of its `serviceTypes` carries the code. A comma-separated list (up to 100) matches a slot carrying any of them.

parameters.name: npi
parameters.description: Filter by the provider's National Provider Identifier: a clinician's, or an organization's when a healthcare service is the provider. Ten digits; a comma-separated list (up to 100) matches a slot whose provider carries any of them. Matched as the publisher sent it, in either NPI identifier system, across every publisher.

parameters.name: specialty
parameters.description: Filter by specialty: a slot matches when its provider's `specialties` or its schedule's `specialties` carry the code. Send `code` to match it in any code system, or `system|code` to match it in that system only. Codes are each publisher's own and are not translated between code systems, so one code finds the publishers that use it; `GET /v1/scheduling/specialties` lists them. A specialty sent as text only cannot be matched. A comma-separated list (up to 100) matches any of them.

parameters.name: appointmentType
parameters.description: Filter by appointment type.

parameters.name: acceptingPatients
parameters.description: Filter to slots accepting patients of this kind (HL7 `accepting-patients` CodeSystem: `newpt` | `existptonly` | `existptfam`). Slots marked `nopt` (not accepting patients) are never served, so `nopt` is not a valid filter value. Lenient: a slot that does not declare an accepting-patients code matches any value (absence never hides a slot); a slot that declares one must equal the requested value.

parameters.name: isVirtual
parameters.description: Filter to virtual (`true`) or in-person (`false`) slots.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: Filter by the location's city.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Filter by the location's state.

parameters.name: startAfter
parameters.description: Only slots starting at or after this instant: ISO 8601 with seconds and an offset, such as `2026-07-06T13:00:00-04:00` or `2026-07-06T17:00:00Z`. A value without seconds is refused. When absent, slots start from now unless `includePast=true`.

parameters.name: startBefore
parameters.description: Only slots starting at or before this instant: ISO 8601 with seconds and an offset, such as `2026-07-06T13:00:00-04:00` or `2026-07-06T17:00:00Z`. A value without seconds is refused.

parameters.name: includePast
parameters.description: Include slots that started before now. Defaults to `false`: with no `startAfter`, results start from now. An explicit `startAfter` applies as given either way.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size: the number of provider locations, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of provider locations to skip for pagination. Defaults to 0.

200.description: The matching provider locations, and their total number before paging.

implementation.description: haau3 platform FHIR R4 API. Four services and two operations are served from this one base: terminology (CodeSystem, ValueSet), the provider directory (Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, OrganizationAffiliation, HealthcareService, Location, Endpoint), questionnaires (Questionnaire), Medical Benefits (InsurancePlan), MedList's reconcile-medications and Pharmacy Benefits' process-message. Note that `/v1/` versions the haau3 platform API contract, not FHIR; the FHIR release is `r4`, and is echoed on every response as the `fhirVersion` media-type parameter.

rest.documentation:
All operations accept GET with query parameters and POST with a Parameters resource. Complex inputs — coding, and codeableConcept on the validate-code operations — are accepted on POST only, as the operations framework requires; on GET pass system and code as separate parameters. A codeableConcept validates if ANY of its codings is a member, which fits data whose elements carry a vendor-local coding alongside a standard one; per-coding membership deliberately ignores each coding's display (a wrong label must not veto a right code — display checking is available on the single-coding form). A coding's version is honoured where the operation defines a version parameter (the CodeSystem operations); ValueSet validation always uses the current code-system version and refuses a versioned coding rather than silently ignoring it. A coding whose system disagrees with an explicitly supplied system or url parameter is refused. Value sets and code systems are addressed by canonical url only; instance-level operation paths ([type]/[id]/$operation) are not offered. An expansion is returned whole: displayLanguage, includeDesignations and activeOnly are refused by name on $expand, and filter, count and offset narrow only a value set this service hosts, being refused for one resolved from its own source. A batch Bundle POSTed to the base runs several operations in one round trip; each entry succeeds or fails independently.

Provider directory resources are proxied from the CMS National Provider Directory and served as published, without modification. Search is GET only. Every search parameter is either declared here or refused by name: a parameter this service does not serve is never silently ignored. Where the directory requires a parameter to be sent beside another (`network` on PractitionerRole and HealthcareService), the rule is applied here, before the directory is asked.

A curated set of questionnaires is served from copies vendored at a recorded release of their source, so those forms render the same way on every request. A search that names a canonical URL this service holds no copy of is answered from the source directly, and depends on that source being reachable. A search with no parameters lists the curated set. Search is GET only, and every search parameter is either declared here or refused by name. No operations are served on Questionnaire, and no QuestionnaireResponse is accepted or stored: a completed response is built by the application that collected it and references the questionnaire as `{url}|{version}`.

Medical Benefits (InsurancePlan): what a Medicare Advantage or ACA Marketplace plan covers and what a member pays, read from the files CMS publishes. Each plan conforms to the haau3 Medical Benefits profile (https://haau3.com/fhir/StructureDefinition/haau3-insurance-plan) and to the SBC InsurancePlan profile of the CARIN Digital Insurance Card guide, 2.0.0-ballot, and names the CMS release it was read from.

MedList: POST [base]/$reconcile-medications reconciles one patient's medication records into one clean list, returned as a Bundle of reconciled MedicationRequests with a Provenance for each. The operation receives patient data, so send it only under an executed agreement. Nothing a request carries is stored or logged. It is invoked directly and is not offered inside a batch.

Pharmacy Benefits: POST [base]/$process-message answers a pharmacy benefit check of the CARIN Consumer Real-Time Pharmacy Benefit Check: what a medication would cost a member under their coverage (event rtpbc-request), or its price at pharmacies near a ZIP code, without patient details (event rtpbc-request-non-phi). A member's request carries patient data, so send it only under an executed agreement. Nothing a request carries is stored or logged. It is invoked directly and is not offered inside a batch.

searchParam.name: identifier
searchParam.documentation: An NPI, as `{system}|{npi}` or a bare 10-digit value. Accepted systems: http://terminology.hl7.org/NamingSystem/npi, http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/us-npi, urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.4.6. All of them resolve the same provider. Responses carry the directory's own system, `http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/us-npi`, which may differ from the one you sent. One NPI per search; use a batch Bundle to resolve several. Any other identifier system is refused by name rather than searched, because a system the source does not index would answer with an empty result that reads as 'no such provider'.

A search with no parameters lists the curated set, the questionnaires this server holds copies of, which are answered from those copies and render the same way on every request. A search naming a canonical `url` this server holds no copy of is answered from the source directly and depends on the source being reachable; when it cannot answer, the response is an OperationOutcome with a 5xx and never an empty searchset. Start the search with `service-category=pharm` (every kind) or `specialty` (one kind or several, separated by commas). A pharmacy search needs `location.address-state` with `location.address-postalcode` or `location.address-city`, or one pharmacy's `organization` or `organization.identifier`; `name` narrows it. Add `_include=HealthcareService:organization` and `_include=HealthcareService:location` to get each pharmacy's organization (its NPI) and store (its address) in the same bundle.

Pharmacies are found in NPPES, CMS's NPI Registry, until CMS's National Provider Directory serves them. Each is found and served at its primary practice address. The organization keeps the directory's own id (`Organization-{NPI}`) and reads back from the directory, where a pharmacy registered in the last few weeks can answer 404 until the directory's next load. A pharmacy service's and store's ids are read back from NPPES, and change when the search moves to the directory. NPPES returns at most 1,200 records for one search, so a continuation past them is refused with a 422 that asks for a narrower search, rather than repeating a page or ending early. One store can bill under more than one NPI, and each is served as its own pharmacy.

With no parameters, this lists the questionnaires this service holds copies of. Those render the same way on every request, and that list is what you can rely on.

Naming a canonical `url` reaches any questionnaire the source publishes, including ones this service holds no copy of. Those depend on the source being reachable, and when it cannot answer you get a `502`, `503` or `504` carrying an `OperationOutcome`, so a failure never arrives looking like an empty result.

A canonical that is the address of a form published at its own address, under `https://smart-health-checkin.org/connectathon/Questionnaire/` or another place this service is set up to reach, is fetched from that address and served exactly as published, its entry's `fullUrl` the address it was fetched from. Any other canonical matches nothing.

Two parameters are offered: `url` (the canonical, optionally as `{url}|{version}`) and `version`. Every other parameter, `status` included, is refused by name rather than ignored, so a search never quietly answers a different question than the one asked. Results are never paged: one page, with `total` set.

Questionnaires are served exactly as their source publishes them. Each carries its own `copyright`, which must be kept with the form wherever it goes.

A canonical that is the address of a form under a place this service is set up to reach is fetched from that address; any other canonical matches nothing.

Search the Medicare Advantage and ACA Marketplace plans being served, by identifier, name, or the state or county a plan is sold in. A search needs at least one of `identifier`, a form of `name`, `coverage-area-state` or `coverage-area-county`; `type` and `sold-to` narrow a search but are not one. Every result is the whole plan, sorted by name and then id, and every page states the total. Follow the `next` link to continue.

A plan sold in only part of a county matches the whole county. `GET /v1/fhir/r4/InsurancePlan/$counties?state=FL` lists a state's counties and their codes.

Every other parameter is refused by name rather than ignored, so a search never quietly answers a different question than the one asked. `address-state` and `address-postalcode` are refused with a pointer to the coverage-area parameters, because in FHIR R4 they search a plan's contact address.

Drug-only and dental-only plans are not served. An identifier search that finds one answers no plan and an `OperationOutcome` entry saying why.

A Medicare Advantage plan by CMS's plan id (`http://cms.gov/medicare/ma-plan-id`, the segment in three digits: `H2406-013-000`) or its bid_id (`https://haau3.com/fhir/NamingSystem/cms-ma-bid-id`: `H2406_013_0`). A Marketplace plan by its HIOS plan id (`https://haau3.com/fhir/NamingSystem/hios-plan-id`: `19898FL0340001-01`) or its standard component (`https://haau3.com/fhir/NamingSystem/hios-standard-component-id`: `19898FL0340001`), which finds every variant.

A code that names no county is refused. Defined by the haau3 implementation guide (`https://haau3.com/fhir/SearchParameter/InsurancePlan-coverage-area-county`).

post.summary: Check what a medication costs (pharmacy benefit check)
post.description: FHIR system-level operation `$process-message`, as the CARIN Consumer Real-Time Pharmacy Benefit Check (STU2 ballot, `2.0.0-ballot`) specifies. Not yet open to customers: while its price sources are being licensed, every request from a customer's organization, with or without patient details, is refused with `403` `forbidden`. POST a FHIR `Bundle` of type `message` whose first entry is a MessageHeader with one of two events. `rtpbc-request-non-phi` asks for a medication's price without patient details: a Claim naming the product (an NDC of 11 digits with no dashes, or an RxNorm code) and the quantity, with the patient and the coverage masked, and a pharmacy, up to three ZIP codes, or both. It is answered by price sources: Cost Plus Drugs (its mail order and the Team Cuban Card) and ClixRx. `rtpbc-request` asks what a medication would cost a member under their coverage: the member's Patient and Coverage, with the payer's identifier in `payor.identifier`, the prescription and its prescriber, and a pharmacy. It is answered by the member's insurer, found by the payer's Payer ID: a `payor.identifier` whose `type` is `payerid` from `http://hl7.org/fhir/us/carin-bb/CodeSystem/C4BBIdentifierType`. An insurer that answers only with the member's own authorization is sent the access token from the member's login with that insurer, in the `Payer-Authorization` header, for that one request; it is never stored, logged or sent anywhere else. No insurer is connected yet. The answer is a `message` Bundle whose MessageHeader answers the request's, with one ClaimResponse that carries either prices and coverage in `item` or the reason there are none in `error`, and for a member's request the request's Patient as it was sent. With prices, `item` is the lowest price at a pharmacy near the ZIP codes or at the pharmacy named, every price is also an `addItem` alternative naming its pharmacy by an Organization in the Bundle and its price source in `programCode`, from `https://haau3.com/fhir/CodeSystem/pharmacy-benefits-price-source`, and `processNote` says where each price came from, when, and which free discount card pays it. Each price repeats the request's product coding, which CARIN requires to carry a display: an RxNorm code sent without one is answered with the display haau3's RxNorm release gives it, and an NDC needs its display sent with it. A check no connected source can answer carries `no-responder-for-coverage`, `no-price-source` or `source-not-available-to-caller` from `https://haau3.com/fhir/CodeSystem/pharmacy-benefits-processing-code`, and a member's request to an insurer that needs the member's authorization carries `payer-authorization-required` when none was sent and `payer-authorization-rejected` when the insurer refused it. A member's request the insurer declines under its own rules carries `insurer-declined-request`, and sending it again gives the same answer. An insurer that prices by NDC is asked about the request's NDC, or, for an RxNorm code, an NDC haau3's RxNorm release holds for the code or one of its branded forms, named in the answer's note; with none held it is not asked and the answer carries `ndc-required`, so send the NDC. A price is an estimate; the pharmacy confirms the price. A member's request receives patient data, so send real patient data only under an executed business associate agreement (BAA) on the Team or Scale plan. Without both, send a member's request only as test data marked as such, the request and every resource in it labelled with the `meta.security` coding `HTEST` from `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v3-ActReason`; anything else is refused with `403` `phi-agreement-required`. A request without patient details needs neither. Nothing a request carries is stored or logged, apart from the request's ids, and every answer is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The operation takes no query parameters and is not offered inside a batch. The contract is published at https://fhir.haau3.com/pharmacy-benefits.html.

It is forwarded once, to that insurer, for this request, and is never stored, logged or sent anywhere else. Without it, such a request is answered `payer-authorization-required`; a token the insurer refuses is answered `payer-authorization-rejected`. A request without patient details that carries it is refused.

XRequestId.description: An id of your own for this request, as a UUID. It comes back in the `X-Correlation-Id` header and is kept with haau3's record of the request. Any value that is not a UUID is ignored. See https://docs.haau3.com/errors#request-ids.
The id haau3 gave this request, a UUID, on every response. Quote it in a question about the response. A problem carries the same id as its `instance`.

XCorrelationId.description: The `X-Request-Id` you sent, when it was a UUID.

bearerAuth.description: Your platform API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`: a live key (`haau3_sk_live_…`) for every service, or a test key (`haau3_sk_test_…`) for the Sandbox, the one place a test key works and a live key does not.

type.description: What kind of problem this is: an anchor on https://docs.haau3.com/errors.

title.description: A short summary, the same for every occurrence of the type.

status.description: The HTTP status code of this response.

detail.description: What went wrong this time, and how to correct it.

instance.description: This request's id as `urn:uuid:<id>`, the same id as the `X-Request-Id` header.

code.description: On a 403: why, as a code from `https://haau3.com/fhir/CodeSystem/api-error`, the same one an OperationOutcome carries in `issue.details.coding`.

issues.description: On a 400: one entry per parameter that is not valid.

path.description: The parameter, or the field within it, that is not valid.
